newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN TO SELL 1-YR BONDS ON AUG 19.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN TO SELL 1-YR BONDS ON AUG 19.

text.p: The Slovak central bank (NBS) said on Wednesday it would auction an unspecified tranche of finance ministry one-year state bonds on August 19.
The bonds will have a nominal value of 100,000 crowns ($2,850) and carry a fixed annual coupon rate of 11.00 percent, the NBS said in a statement.
The ministry does not set an amount on offer at state securities auctions or set a minimum or maximum limit price on bids.
The ministry sold a 1.120-billion crown tranche of one-year state bonds on August 5 with an average yield at 19.388 percent, up from 17.8 percent in the last sale of similar bonds on July 22.

The finance ministry uses T-bills and state bonds as the main tools to cover the state budget deficit, which widened to 17.936 billion crowns in the first seven months of the year from 13.209 billion in the January-June period of 1997.
